cohort: The study analyzed data from health facilities and administrative offices regarding women who used antenatal care services in 2014.
finding: The mHealth program, particularly when incorporating demand-side generation for facility births, was cost-effective (US$9,806 per life saved) in reducing mortality among women, neonates, and stillbirths.
mod_finding: Improved labor and delivery during facility delivery, encouraged by the mHealth program, significantly contributed to mortality reductions and enhanced the program's cost-effectiveness.
